log.note: Bootstrap. Spec + immutable plan frozen. Scaffold staged. Awaiting first-push human clearance (Rule 8).

STEP 0 DONE. Kicked off manually (bridge up, neil-cipher authed w/ workflow scope). gh repo create neil-cipher/sketchflow --public --push; commit 22db207 as neil-cipher <295313991+...>; GitHub Actions CI SUCCESS 14s. Next: step 1 (synthetic Zipfian generator + exact baseline).

STEP 1 DONE inline (user: build every day, no date-waiting). Zipfian stream + ExactCounter + 4 tests; commit 3a8d5a1; CI green 12s. GENTLE date-gating REMOVED from the job. Page redesigned: Ansh-style step-by-step build log w/ badges + commands; bullets-only Explainer.

STEP 2 DONE. Tabulation hashing (Zobrist 1970; Patrascu&Thorup J.ACM 2012), k independent seedable functions; fairness gates (uniform chi2 + independence). Tests caught a py3.11 tuple-seed TypeError pre-push. Commit 7b1ca0a; CI green 17s. Next: step 3 Bloom warm-up.

STEP 3 DONE. BloomFilter on step-2 HashFamily; gates: zero false negatives (absolute) + measured FPR vs analytic (1-e^{-kn/m})^k (Bloom, CACM 1970). 11 tests green. Commit 3208dae; CI 12s. Next: step 4 Bloom sizing calculator.

STEP 4 DONE. size_bloom(n, target_fpr) -> (m,k): m=ceil(-n ln p/ln^2 2), best-of-floor/ceil k, plus promise-keeping m-bump (k-rounding left analytic 0.01004>0.01 - a sizing calculator must deliver its promise exactly). Gate: analytic <= target exactly + measured FPR within 3-sigma on 50k probes. Commit ad72e7c.

STEP 5 DONE. CountMinSketch(width,depth,seed) on the step-2 HashFamily: depth x width counter matrix, weighted add, row_values. Gate: never-undercount invariant for every key of a 10k Zipfian stream vs ExactCounter under heavy collisions (width 256/8). 20 tests green. Commit e2df3f4, CI 19s. Next: step 6 min-query + eps/delta sizing -> first green tag.

STEP 6 DONE. query()=min(row_values) + size_cms(eps,delta)->(ceil(e/eps),ceil(ln(1/delta))). Gate: per-key failure rate ≤ δ across 300 seeds on 10k Zipfian stream (top-10 heavy hitters each checked). 28 tests green. Commit 1e6bae1, CI 34s. Tag green-sketchflow-1 cut (7 green steps 0-6). Next: step 7 memory accounting + serialize/deserialize.

STEP 7 DONE. bytes_used() via recursive sys.getsizeof (honest Python overhead) + to_bytes()/from_bytes() compact binary serialization (24-byte header + depth*width*8 counters). Gate: bytes_used == independent measurement; round-trip preserves every query and row_values; blob size == 24+d*w*8; corrupt blobs raise ValueError. 38 tests green. Commit 9912643, CI 35s. Next: step 8, CMS inner-product / join-size estimate.

STEP 8 DONE. inner_product(other) = min over rows of row-wise dot product (Cormode & Muthukrishnan 2005, Section 3). Validates dimension+seed match. Gate: 200 seeds, two 5k Zipfian streams, violation rate (est - true > ε·N_a·N_b) ≤ 3·δ. Also: never undercounts, symmetric, self-join ≈ L2², disjoint streams bounded, weighted adds correct. 11 new tests, 49 total green. Commit 51397cc, CI 52s. Next: step 9, conservative-update CMS.

STEP 9 DONE. ConservativeUpdateCMS subclass: overrides add() to only bump counters at or below the current minimum estimate (Estan & Varghese, SIGCOMM 2002, §4.2). Gate: for every key on a 10k Zipfian stream, CU estimate ≤ plain-CMS estimate AND CU estimate ≥ true count (never undercounts). Also: total CU overestimation strictly < plain CMS (by >20%), weighted adds correct, inherited inner_product/serialize/bytes_used all work, round-trip preserves state. 12 new tests, 61 total green. Commit 604496b, CI 54s. Next: step 10, Space-Saving top-k.

STEP 10 DONE. SpaceSaving(k) — bounded-memory heavy hitter tracker: at most k monitored counters; when full, evicts the minimum-count entry and the newcomer inherits evicted_count+1 (Metwally, Agrawal & El Abbadi, ICDT 2005). Gate: on Zipfian streams with heavy hitters above the N/k threshold, every such key is present in the monitored set; top-k keys match the exact baseline; monitored estimates are always ≥ true counts (overestimate). Also: eviction mechanics, weighted adds, k=1 edge case, capacity never exceeded, tie-breaking deterministic. 19 new tests, 80 total green. Commit 1b8eb2b, CI 54s. Next: step 11, Space-Saving min-heap + hash index for O(log k) update.

STEP 11 DONE. SpaceSaving internals upgraded to min-heap (heapq) + hash index for O(log k) add() — same external API, same results, faster at large k. Heap entries are [count, seq, key] lists; seq monotonic for FIFO tie-breaking; _index dict maps key→entry for O(1) lookup. Bump = update count in-place + sift-down; eviction = overwrite root + sift-down. _assert_heap_invariant() verifies heap property + index↔counters consistency. Gate: all step-10 behavioral tests still pass (guarantee, overestimate, eviction, top-k ordering); heap invariant holds after every mutation pattern (inserts, bumps, evictions, weighted, k=1); throughput at k=2000 stays >15% of k=50 (O(log k) scaling confirmed). 16 new tests, 96 total green. Commit 139b17b, CI 53s. Next: step 12, CMS + Space-Saving combined engine.

STEP 12 DONE. SketchEngine class in engine.py — composes CMS (or CU-CMS) + SpaceSaving into a single-pass analytics engine. Auto-sizes CMS from (ε,δ) via size_cms(). API: add(key), estimate(key) → CMS query, heavy_hitters(n) → Space-Saving top-k keys with CMS-estimated counts (tighter than raw SS counts), summary(). Supports conservative=True for CU-CMS variant. Gate: end-to-end on Zipfian streams, engine top-10 matches exact top-10 across 10 seeds; CMS estimates used (not SS counts); CU mode reduces overestimation; totals in sync across CMS+SS; weighted adds; edge cases (empty, single, k=1); validation. 18 new tests, 114 total green. Commit 099e86f, CI 50s. Phase P3 complete. Next: step 13, benchmark harness v1 (Phase P4).

STEP 13 DONE. bench.py benchmark harness v1 — runs seeded Zipfian streams through CMS, CU-CMS, Engine, Engine-CU; measures per-key error (mean/max/p99 absolute, mean relative) and memory (bytes_used, baseline_bytes, ratio) against ExactCounter ground truth; writes report/results.csv. CLI: PYTHONPATH=src python -m sketchflow.bench. First run (50k stream, 3 epsilons, 4 variants = 12 rows): CU-CMS halves mean error vs plain CMS; at ε=0.001 sketch memory exceeds dict baseline (honest Python overhead). 14 new tests, 128 total green. Commit 0bd3355, CI 44s. Phase P4 started. Next: step 14, accuracy-vs-memory sweep (vary width/depth, plot error decay via matplotlib).

STEP 14 DONE. sweep.py sweeps ε over two orders of magnitude (0.1→0.0005, 8 points × 4 variants = 32 rows → report/sweep.csv). plot.py reads CSV and generates report/accuracy_vs_memory.png via matplotlib (headless Agg backend): two log-log panels (mean error & max error vs sketch memory), four lines per panel (CMS, CU-CMS, Engine, Engine-CU). Gate: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m sketchflow.plot` regenerates the PNG from CSV in one command. Key finding visualised: CU-CMS halves mean error at every memory point; error decays ~linearly on log-log as ε shrinks. CI fix: added matplotlib to pip install in ci.yml. 15 new tests, 143 total green. Commits d12a237+f1d955c, CI 67s. Next: step 15, HUMAN fetch CIC-IDS-2017 CSV.

STEP 15 DONE. CIC-IDS-2017 dataset fetched from UNB official site (cicresearch.ca). MachineLearningCSV.zip (224 MB, 8 day-CSVs, 79 CICFlowMeter features + Label). Stratified sample from Thursday-Morning-WebAttacks: 10,180 rows (2,180 attacks — Brute Force 1507, XSS 652, SQL Injection 21 — + 8,000 random benign, seed 42) → data/cicids_sample.csv (2.94 MB). SHA256: 2b22481f8f5bbd6f9f0f36f1bbc99c738c42d9033dfe63f2a3205a2f6eedd311. Human block cleared. Commit 5f4b7f2, CI green 74s. Next: step 16, CIC-IDS loader → parse flow keys from real intrusion-detection data.

STEP 16 DONE. cicids.py loader: load_cicids() yields 'port:N' stream keys from CIC-IDS-2017 ML-format CSV (Destination Port is the only network-header column — no raw IPs). load_cicids_flows() yields rich dicts (port, label, duration, packet counts). Next: step 18 (MAWI pcap → flow-key stream via dpkt, engine on backbone traffic).

STEP 18 DONE. mawi.py loader: parses MAWI pcap with dpkt, extracts 5-tuple flow keys (src_ip:port->dst_ip:port/PROTO) from Ethernet/IP packets. Non-IP packets (262/10000) skipped. 9738 IP packets yield 4319 distinct flow keys. Protocol mix: TCP 8022 (82%), UDP 1256 (13%), ICMP 319, GRE 141. Truncated-TCP handling: packets where snaplen=96 clips the transport header still get TCP label (ports=0). Top flow: 197.201.32.208->197.201.34.164/GRE (106 pkts, a GRE tunnel). Engine top-10 matches exact baseline with k=500. CU-CMS reduces overestimation vs plain CMS on backbone traffic. Never-undercount invariant holds for all 4319 flows. dpkt added to CI pip install. 22 new tests, 182 total green. Commit b20ca37, CI green. Next: step 19 (adversary v1: collision-maximising input).

STEP 19 DONE. adversary.py — Phase P5 opens. Threat model: known-seed/white-box attacker (Crosby & Wallach, USENIX Security 2003 hash-flooding model) who knows a CMS's exact (width,depth,seed) brute-force-searches for keys sharing the SAME bucket in EVERY row ('full-row collision group'); find_colliding_group() does this search (candidates f'{namespace}-{i}', deterministic/reproducible). adversarial_stream() builds N disjoint collision groups and replays each key; random_control_stream() is the benign comparison at identical size. Gate result across 25 seeds on a deliberately small demo sketch (width=16, depth=3): adversarial stream beat the benign control's mean overestimation error on 25/25 seeds (100%); mean adversarial error 81.60 vs mean control error 11.33 — a 7.2x ratio. Flip-side check: against a production-sized sketch (size_cms(0.01,0.05) = width 272, depth 3), the same search fails within 5,000 trials — confirming the attack needs a small/known-seed sketch, not a break of correctly-sized deployments. 9 new tests, 191 total green. Commit 3352e4a, CI green 59s. Next: step 20 (guarantee-violation meter: empirical P(error > epsilon*N) vs promised delta).

STEP 20 DONE. guarantee_meter.py — turns the eps/delta check into a reusable meter: violating_keys()/violation_rate() flag any key whose CMS estimate exceeds true+eps*N; benign_violation_study() reruns step 6's 300-hash-seed check as a general utility; adversarial_violation_study() applies the identical meter to a step-19 collision stream. Benign result: at eps=0.01, delta=0.05, 300 trials, 10k Zipfian stream — all 10 top-heavy-hitter keys measured 0.0 empirical violation rate (well inside the delta=0.05 promise; margin cutoff 3*delta=0.15 per step-6's established sampling-noise allowance). Adversarial result: on the step-19 demo sketch (width=16,depth=3,seed=42, 5 groups x 5 keys x 20 events, eps=0.02) the collision-maximising stream hit 100% violation rate (1.0) vs 48% (0.48) for the size-matched benign control — same meter, decisively higher failure rate once the attacker knows the seed. 6 new tests, 197 total green. Commit e7c3a28, CI green 1m0s. Next: step 21 (CU vs plain CMS under adversarial load — does conservative update survive the attack; report/adversarial.csv).

STEP 21 DONE. adversarial_study.py — runs {plain CMS, CU-CMS} x {step-19 adversarial stream, size-matched benign control} across 10 hash seeds at identical (width,depth,seed) memory; measures each cell with the step-20 meter; ships report/adversarial.csv (40 rows, regenerable via PYTHONPATH=src python -m sketchflow.adversarial_study). CORE FINDING: conservative update does NOT survive the attack — against full-row collision groups CU degenerates into plain CMS (every group member shares the same bucket in every row, so CU's add() finds min == all group cells and bumps them in lock-step; no cleaner row left to trust). Numbers (demo sketch 16x3, eps=0.02): adversarial — plain violation 1.000 / mean_error 82.00, CU 1.000 / 80.04 (97.6% of plain, no rescue). Benign control — plain 0.464 / 11.04, CU 0.000 / 2.00 (step 9's edge intact). Robustness comes from sizing + secret seed, not CU. Reconcile note: code found complete-but-uncommitted in working tree (prior run died pre-commit, 12-Aug pattern); all 204 tests verified green locally then committed. 7 new tests, 204 total green. Commit d4ffde6, CI green 1m40s. Tag green-sketchflow-3 cut. Next: step 22 (adversary on real traces: replay MAWI/CIC with heavy-hitter amplification, report/real_adversarial.png).

STEP 22 DONE. real_adversary.py + real_plot.py — brings adversarial stress to the two REAL traces (MAWI backbone pcap, CIC-IDS-2017 flows) under a weaker/realistic threat model than the known-seed collision attacker of steps 19-21: heavy-hitter amplification (volumetric DDoS pattern). amplify_stream() multiplies the top-10 heavy flows by a factor; the attacker does NOT know the seed and cannot pick colliding keys — only floods flows that are already heavy. Sweeps factor {1,2,5,10,20,50} x provisioning {eps=0.01 sized w=272, eps=0.1 under-provisioned w=28}. Gate artifact report/real_adversarial.png (+ .csv, 24 rows), regenerable via PYTHONPATH=src python -m sketchflow.real_plot. CORE FINDING — 'which promise breaks': a well-sized CMS is essentially immune to amplification on real traffic (MAWI mean err 22.2->23.0 at x50; CIC dead flat 3.34 — amplified top ports sit in uncontested buckets; provisioned violation ~0). Under-provisioning breaks the operator's FIXED baseline promise eps*N0: MAWI 0 -> 3.4% of keys, CIC 0.07% -> 2.4% by x50; mean err climbs (CIC 49.6->163). The SELF-SCALING textbook bound eps*N (N=live length) holds everywhere (theorem violation <=0.0009 max), because it loosens as fast as N grows — volume alone doesn't break the theorem. Invariant proven per row: violation_rate_theorem <= violation_rate_provisioned (since N>=N0 => eps*N>=eps*N0). Robustness = provision for peak / re-size under load, not the theorem. 16 new tests (incl. real-trace integration), 220 total green. Commit c175244, CI green 2m3s. Phase P5 (Adversarial stress — the standout) COMPLETE. Next: step 23 (Phase P6 — Empirical study report v1 in Markdown: method, curves, adversarial findings, honest limits, every claim cited).

STEP 23 DONE. report/EMPIRICAL_STUDY.md — the empirical study written up in full: method (structures/workloads/meter), benign accuracy-vs-memory curves (CU halves error at every memory point; honest finding that pure-Python sketch memory exceeds the dict baseline at eps<=0.001), benign delta-promise study (0.0 violation across 300 seeds), white-box collision attack (CU is NOT a defense — degenerates into plain CMS under full-row collisions; defense = sizing + secret seed), and real-trace volumetric amplification (well-sized sketch immune at x50; under-provisioning breaks the fixed eps*N0 promise at 3.4%/2.4% of keys while the self-scaling theorem bound holds everywhere, max 0.0009). Seven honest-limits paragraphs (toy-sketch attack scope, CPython memory overhead, sample sizes, 2006 MAWI vintage, workload-shape coverage, no CU-literature claim). 9 primary-source references ([CM05][EV02][MAE05][B70][CW03][Z70][PT12][MAWI][CIC17]); every regeneration command listed. Gate: 10 new tests verify presence, sections, citation-key closure (every [X] cited is defined in References), referenced artifacts exist on disk, regen commands present, and headline numbers MATCH the committed CSVs (report cannot drift from data). 230 total green. Commit 297f8f2, CI green 2m6s. Phase P6 started. Next: step 24 (one-command reproducibility: make reproduce + CI job running it clean).

Makefile `reproduce` target runs every artifact generator in dependency order (bench->results.csv, sweep->sweep.csv, plot->accuracy_vs_memory.png, adversarial_study->adversarial.csv, real_plot->real_adversarial.{csv,png}) with PYTHONPATH=src; ci.yml gains a second `reproduce` job: make clean (wipe every generated CSV/PNG) -> make reproduce -> full pytest, so every push proves the whole empirical study regenerates from seeds on a bare checkout and the regenerated data still passes the step-23 report-consistency gates.
